newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, Sept up with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, Sept up with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still mixed late Thursday in moderate activity, with reports of firmer cash prices and bullish inventory data briefly driving spot-September through resistance.

At 1340 EDT, September was still up by 3.6 cents at $2.197 per million British thermal units after earlier piercing resistance with a brief move to $2.205. October was four cents higher at $2.195. Others were mixed, with some late 1998 and 1999 contracts down slightly.

"We got a reaction to the (bullish) AGA number and the cash, but now what? The next two months are shoulder months and I just don't see how we're going to sustain an up market," said one East Coast trader.

Traders agreed Wednesday's inventory data showing an unexpectedly-light weekly stock build of 60 bcf caught many by surprise and helped back today's gains. But they said other supportive factors may be at work.
They said the growing gap to 1994 and 1995 storage levels, now running at a 360-450 bcf deficit, also could lend some support to prices during the typically-soft demand shoulder period.
In addition, they said bears were not likely to be aggressive anytime soon, with the potential for another heat wave or hurricane next month.

And technical traders, while agreeing September was still officially range bound, said a September close today above $2.20 could quickly turn sentiment bullish and force the bears to cover, particularly with cash firm and a brief warm up ahead.

Chart traders saw next resistance in September at the $2.27 double top. Minor supprt was pegged along the short-term up trendline in the $2.10 area, with more important support expected at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045.

Warmer Midwest and Northeast weather is expected into the weekend, but cooler air is forecast for early next week. Temperatures in Florida and Texas are expected to stay close to normal for the period, Weather Services Corp said.

In the cash Thursday, early-August Gulf Coast gas firmed a few cents to about the $2.20 level. August Midcon gained almost five cents to the $2.12-2.15 area. New York city gate gas held relatively steady in the low-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 25,950 contracts traded at 1305 EDT.
On the KCBT, September climbed two cents to $2.085, while deferreds were steady to 2.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.6 cents to 11.2 cents (NYMEX premium).
